character.name: Eleanor Hartley
character.description:
Your name is Eleanor Hartley. You are 64 years old, a woman, and for thirty-one of those years you were the organist at St. Aldric's, where everyone knew the Hartley pew by name.

You loved your son, Daniel. You loved him the way you loved the organ — completely, and on your terms. When Daniel was nineteen, he told you that Father Whitcombe had been touching him since he was twelve. He told you in the church parking lot, and he was crying, and you were holding the hymnals for Sunday.

You told Daniel he was confused. You told him Father Whitcombe had baptized him. You told your husband Gerald that Daniel was using drugs again, and Gerald believed you, because you had never lied to Gerald about anything except this.

Daniel went to the diocese. The diocese called you, and you told them Daniel had a history of instability — you even sent them his prescription records from Dr. Peshwani. The case was closed. Father Whitcombe stayed at St. Aldric's for nine more years.

Daniel stopped calling. Gerald died believing his son was a liar. When Daniel was twenty-six, he drove to the church, sat in the parking lot, and took the pills from his prescription records, the ones you had used as evidence of his instability.

You organized the funeral. You played the organ yourself. Two hundred people watched you sob through "Be Still, My Soul," and every one of them thought: what a mother. What devotion. Daniel's hospital roommate, Marcus Lee, came up to you afterward and said Daniel had told him everything, and you took his hand and said Daniel never stopped being sick, and Marcus Lee looked ashamed, and you let him.

You kept Daniel's diary in your nightstand. You never burned it. You just never opened it.

Last March, alone in the house, you went to the nightstand and opened it to the first page.

You were still holding it when the pain reached your arm.

prompts.character_user:
You have died and gone to hell to be tortured for all eternity, for a deadly sin you
committed.

Your name: Eleanor Hartley
Age: 64
Gender: female

Write the story of your life, ending with how you died. No longer than 300 words. Start the story by
stating your name, gender and age.

Who did you love?
How did your sin destroy them?
What lie did you have to tell yourself and others to keep going?
What kind of person do you want people to think you are?
What secret would make everyone see you for what you really are?
prompts.name_user: Invent one full name — first name and surname — for a person aged {AGE}, {GENDER}. Any background. Reply with the name and nothing else: no explanation, no punctuation, no quotation marks.
prompts.craft_suffix:
Write in the second person — "you," not "she/he/they." Name every person you mention, and
keep using their name rather than he, she, they or them.

Stop at the moment of your death. Do not describe arriving anywhere, and do not describe
the room.

End on a fact, not on what it meant. The last sentence is an event or a detail — not a
verdict, and not a line telling us what you knew, believed, or refused to admit. Leave
that for the others in the room to find out.
